comments.content: `terminalWidth` is declared but never assigned, so it is always 0 and the `terminalWidth >= 80` branch is dead code. This means the pretty/column-aligned output path is never taken. If this is intentional for now (pending `sys.getWidthOfTerminal`), consider removing the dead branch or adding a TODO; otherwise wire up the terminal width.

`showAdditionalInfoOutput` dereferences `valueCandidates.possibleValues` without a nil check, but `getValueCandidate` returns `nil` for `CommandLineOptionTypeObject`. Callers pass the result of `getValueCandidate` directly, so this will panic for object-typed options. Add a nil guard at the top of the function (e.g. `if valueCandidates == nil { return false }`).

`option.DefaultValueDescription` is compared against string literals `"false"` and `"n/a"`, but elsewhere in this file it is treated as a `*diagnostics.Message` (see the type assertion in `generateOptionOutput`). Comparing a `*diagnostics.Message` to a string will never be true, so this branch is effectively dead. Compare against the formatted message text instead.

`getPossibleValues` returns `string(option.Kind)` for string/number/boolean options, which yields the raw enum value (e.g. `"string"`, `"number"`, `"boolean"`). This happens to match the baseline output, but it is fragile: it relies on the enum's string representation matching the user-facing type name. Consider mapping explicitly to `"string"`/`"number"`/`"boolean"` to avoid breakage if the enum values change.

`inverted.Set(value, append(inverted.GetOrZero(value), name))` — `GetOrZero` returns the zero value (`nil` slice) when the key is absent, and `append(nil, name)` is fine, but if the same `value` appears multiple times the returned slice is appended to and re-set, which is correct. However, note that `GetOrZero` may return a shared backing array; verify `OrderedMap.GetOrZero` semantics to ensure no aliasing bug when the same value is set repeatedly.
